text: Lynn Conway was born in Mount Vernon, New York, in 1938. Raised as a boy, she experienced gender dysphoria and attempted a gender transition in her youth, which was met with social and medical challenges. After being fired from IBM in 1968 for revealing her intention to transition, she restarted her career in stealth mode, working in computer design and architecture at companies like Memorex and Xerox PARC. At Xerox, she co-founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology and co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* with Carver Mead, a foundational textbook in chip design. She pioneered dimensionless, scalable design rules and developed the MOSIS system, a prototype for rapid prototyping and short-run fabrication of chip designs, which became a cornerstone of the VLSI design industry. Conway joined DARPA in 1983 and later the University of Michigan, where she specialized in visual communications and control systems. She is widely recognized for her contributions to the design of VLSI systems, earning numerous awards including the IEEE EAB Major Educational Innovation Award, Fellow of the IEEE, and induction into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2023. In addition to her technical achievements, Conway is a prominent advocate for transgender rights, having publicly shared her story and worked to promote inclusion and understanding of gender identity in the tech industry. She died on June 9, 2024, at the age of 86.
